accuracy.evidence: Checked against the National Curriculum Year 4 Electricity programme of study (identify common appliances that run on electricity; guidance: pupils should be taught about precautions for working safely with electricity). UK mains is 230 V nominal and US 120 V, an AA cell is 1.5 V, so the lab's 'over 100 volts' bar is true in both countries. Overhead lines arc across gaps (Energy Networks Association 'Look Out Look Up'). Button batteries burn tissue within about 2 hours (RoSPA/CAPT). p2, p3, m5 and m7 give whole positive answers at every range corner (m7 min is 4-3=1).

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented child beliefs that all electricity is like a toy battery (step 2 prediction 'They are the same', m1), that wet hands are fine if you are quick (step 3 prediction, p4, challenge wet-hands question), that pulling the cable is the same as pulling the plug (step 5 prediction 'Either one is fine', m2) and that a kite only matters if it touches the wire (step 6, m4). The adult text names each of these under Common mistakes.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagzap is the only lab about electrical hazards and safe actions: sort mains versus battery, compare voltages, dry hands and move a hairdryer, find three kitchen dangers, unplug in the right order and fly a kite away from power lines. flagcond tests which materials conduct in a circuit and never touches safety; the 30% shingle gate passed against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Every idea is learned by doing: the strength bars only fill after the child taps Test the battery and Test the wall socket, the sink scene only turns safe after the towel and the hairdryer are both used, the unplug step gives an oops if Pull the cable is chosen and only lights Done after Switch off then Pull the plug, and the kite must be dragged into the open park box before the step completes.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options taken from how 6 and 7 year olds talk about plugs: 'A small battery and a wall socket. Which one is stronger?' (They are the same), 'Your hands are wet. Is it OK to touch a plug if you are quick?' (Yes, if you are quick) and 'To unplug a lamp, what do you hold?' (Either one is fine). Each is answered by the task that follows it.

challenge_feedback.evidence: The Challenge step cycles six mixed questions (stronger source, wet hands before a switch, toast stuck in a toaster, how to unplug a lamp, kite in a power line, cable with wires showing) and rotates the answer order each time. Each wrong option has its own why() message, twelve m= lines in all, e.g. 'Be very quick' explains that speed does not help because water carries electricity straight away.

readability.evidence: Kid text measures FK grade 3.4 (target 5.0 for family) with one idea per short sentence, and the adult text 7.1 (target 10.0). Lab prompts stay under fifteen words, e.g. 'Switch off at the wall. Then hold the plug and pull.' Curriculum words kept exact: mains electricity, socket, plug, cable, switch, appliance, battery, electric shock.

no_filler.evidence: No praise padding or 'let's explore' openers; every lab line either instructs or explains a hazard. The adult paragraphs give the curriculum source, the volts and water science, named common mistakes, then what each lab step does, with no repeated sentences between kid text, captions and feedback.

mobile.evidence: Walked on iPhone 13 emulation in light and dark: all seven steps fit the 390 px width, item tiles in the sort and spot steps are about 70 px squares, every action is also a full-width button under the canvas, the kite drag works by touch and by the 'Fly it in the open park' button, and Show me completed every task on phone and desktop.

accessibility.evidence: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme on desktop or phone; the canvas has an aria-label that changes per step, every canvas action has a real button twin, feedback goes to a polite live region, sound has an off toggle, and canvas labels use the theme text colour at weight 800 so Sink and Hairdryer read clearly on both backgrounds.
